gotchas.text: Tool calling needs SGLang with the minicpm5 tool-call parser (sgl-project/sglang#25600). The openbmb cookbook says to install SGLang from main because v0.5.12.post1 lacked it; the PyPI 0.5.20 wheel used here ships it, so no source build is needed any more. The model writes XML tool calls (<function name="x"><param name="k">v</param></function>) and they come back as OpenAI tool_calls with finish_reason tool_calls, with thinking on and off.

SGLang has no MiniCPM5 reasoning parser, but the model uses plain <think> ... </think>, so --reasoning-parser qwen3 splits it into reasoning_content. With enable_thinking left unset the template adds no <think> prefix; the model opens the tag itself and the qwen3 parser still catches it.

flashinfer JIT-compiles its prefill kernels on the first request and shells out to ninja. In a venv that is not activated the first prefill dies with FileNotFoundError: ninja and the scheduler exits; put the venv bin directory on PATH before starting the server.
In a llama.cpp deployment the card warns that the default min_p 0.05 causes repetition and asks for min_p 0; the SGLang default min_p is already 0.

Accuracy here is well above the same suite with thinking left on, and the reason is truncation rather than better code: in the thinking-on row 53 of its 56 misses are items that hit the 4,096-token budget, and all 53 have an empty prediction because the model was still inside <think> and never emitted a function. The misses that remain in this row are genuine wrong code, not scoring artefacts - complete, well-formed functions that fail the suite's tests. Thinking does help where it finishes: at least one item this row gets wrong is one the thinking-on row solved in 1,416 tokens. Read the pair together, not this row alone.

Environment SGLANG_ALLOW_OVERWRITE_LONGER_CONTEXT_LEN=1 and SGLANG_DISABLE_CUDNN_CHECK=1 as the MiniCPM SGLang cookbook recommends, the venv bin directory on PATH (flashinfer JIT needs ninja). Server flags follow the openbmb SGLang cookbook (docs/deployment/sglang.md): --dtype bfloat16 --context-length 131072 --tool-call-parser minicpm5, plus --reasoning-parser qwen3 so the <think> block lands in reasoning_content; --mem-fraction-static 0.75 instead of the cookbook 0.85 to leave the unified-memory box about 20 GB of host headroom (the KV pool still holds about 2 million tokens). Radix prefix cache, chunked prefill 8192, CUDA graphs and the flashinfer attention backend are SGLang defaults. Every request sets temperature 0 and seed 42 as the workloads specify. The chat template has three thinking states: enable_thinking true prefills <think>, false prefills an empty think block, and unset lets the model decide, which on almost every prompt means it thinks. Speed and long-context depth rows send chat_template_kwargs enable_thinking false; eval and needle rows leave it unset (the template default). Load: weights 35.8 s, then CUDA graph capture; SGLang reported max_total_num_tokens 2,035,807 and chunked_prefill_size 8192, and the box had about 21 GB of host memory available after start. max_running_requests is passed explicitly as 512 (the SGLang default on this box was 4096) so the concurrency limit is recorded in the row args and can be read back from /get_server_info. Thinking OFF row. MiniCPM5 thinks by default, and on this suite more than 10 % of the items ran into the output-token budget mid-thought, which scores them wrong however good the model is. This row repeats the same suite with chat_template_kwargs {"enable_thinking": false} and everything else identical; the default-thinking row is kept alongside it, and the pair is the measurement. Accuracy here is not comparable to a model that has no thinking mode to turn off.
